column1: # prerename-leak-verdicts.tsv — single source of truth for the per-path
# migrate-vs-allowlist VERDICT TABLE the temperloop#165 foundation->temperloop
# rename recorded (PR #487 body Sec. (a); CHANGELOG.md "[Unreleased] —
# BREAKING" section), consumed by check-prerename-leak-guard.sh (temperloop
# #433, gate-sweep item) so a pre-rename identifier can migrate/allowlist
# ONLY per an explicit, reviewed row here — never by a silent new occurrence.
# Format: <kind> TAB <token> TAB <verdict> TAB <rationale>
#   kind     — "env" (a FOUNDATION_<NAME> environment-variable identifier,
#              matched by check-prerename-leak-guard.sh's
#              `FOUNDATION_[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*` scan) or "path-leaf" (the final
#              path segment of a `foundation/<leaf>` XDG-rooted machine-state
#              subdir, matched by the guard's `foundation/<leaf>` scan).
#   token    — exact identifier (env) or exact leaf segment (path-leaf).
#              Case-sensitive, matched verbatim.
#   verdict  — "refusal" (the read is GONE, but the literal survives inside
#              the post-window legible refusal or stale-artifact diagnostic
#              that replaced it — the identifier has to be named for the
#              failure to tell the operator WHAT to migrate; permanent, and
#              the only place a pre-rename identifier may still appear in
#              live code), "allowlist" (a grandfathered path the rename item
#              deliberately did NOT migrate — no removal date, stays until a
#              later coordinated-move item revisits it), or "no-action"
#              (matches the FOUNDATION_ shape but is not a stranger-facing
#              config surface at all — an internal script/test-local variable
#              name; nothing to migrate or allowlist, listed defensively so
#              it doesn't read as an unreviewed gap).
#              The former "windowed" verdict (a migrate-with-read-old compat
#              literal, legitimate only through the v0.19.0 removal window)
#              is RETIRED: that window closed in v0.19.0, every read it
#              covered is deleted, and its 8 rows were removed with it. A
#              literal that legitimately outlived the window because a
#              refusal or diagnostic names it carries "refusal" instead. Do
#              not reintroduce "windowed" without a new, dated window.
#   rationale — why, citing the verdict-table row it encodes (PR #487 Sec.
#              (a)) or the CHANGELOG "Grandfathered machine-state paths"
#              paragraph, so a fix is obvious without re-deriving it here.
# NOT covered here (verdict "no-action", no row needed — no FOUNDATION_-shaped
# or foundation/-shaped literal exists for either): KS_LIB_DIR (name-neutral;
# claude/hooks/*'s BASH_SOURCE-relative climb has no foundation-named default
# at all, temperloop#406).
# The compat shim's OWN two remaining intentional legacy literal FORMS —
# the committed per-repo dir (any `.foundation/<leaf>`, e.g. .foundation/config,
# .foundation/baseline.jsonl, .foundation/report.d, .foundation/.gitignore,
# .foundation/.recovery.json — verdict-table row "Committed .foundation/
# per-repo dir") and the CLI compat shim's own binary path
# (`bin/foundation`) — are NOT enumerated here as rows: they are always
# sanctioned by check-prerename-leak-guard.sh's own pattern logic (matched
# unconditionally, no per-leaf lookup) — see that script's header for the two
# unconditional-pass rules. Both forms OUTLIVE the v0.19.0 window close by
# design: `temperloop eject`/`uninstall` still clean legacy residue (that is
# their job), the report-offer age probe still READS an un-migrated repo's
# legacy baseline read-only, and `bin/foundation` stays as a legible
# tombstone so a pre-v0.19.0 install's leftover PATH symlink refuses with a
# message instead of dangling. What the window governed — which dir the CLI
# RESOLVES CONFIG FROM and WRITES — now refuses legibly instead.
env
